subject: Order Form redlines: pricing ladder, min commit, invoicing & tax allocation
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finnova.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: Accounts Payable <ap@finnova.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Draft order form – a few redlines and tax question

Diego,

Thanks for sending over the draft order form. Our legal and finance teams reviewed and returned a couple of marked-up items (attached). High level:

- Pricing ladder: we see the staircase on page 2 but would like confirmation that the discounts are applied to committed units only (not post-commit overage).
- Minimum commit: we need the ability to re-phase the commit after quarter 2 if usage materially undershoots (we proposed a 25% step-down).
- Net terms: AP asked if Redwood can accept Net 60 for EU entities (they can’t do Net 45).
- Invoicing split: they prefer 2 invoices (upfront credit + quarterly true-ups) rather than one consolidated invoice.
- VAT / withholding: we flagged a clause that places VAT responsibility on the customer — please confirm Redwood will provide VAT invoices and supply the appropriate tax IDs.

Attached: Finnova_OrderForm_Redlines_v1.pdf (redline) and a short spreadsheet with the proposed invoice cadence. Can you confirm next steps? We’re hoping to close by end of next week.

Best,
Oliver
Oliver Grant
Head of Procurement, Finnova Systems

[Attachment: Finnova_OrderForm_Redlines_v1.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: Redline_Summary_Table.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finnova.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 12:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Draft order form – a few redlines and tax question

Oliver — thanks for the redlines and clear summary. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Ben (commercials / finance) so we can align quickly.

Immediate answers up front:
- Discounts: our standard is to apply pricing tiers to committed units; overages bill at the overage rate unless you explicitly purchase additional committed units. We can call this out in the pricing appendix.
- VAT: Redwood will issue VAT-compliant invoices to EU customers; we’ll need Finnova’s VAT ID for the invoice header and to confirm reverse charge applicability.

Kimberly / Ben — see attachments from Oliver. Can we get a short note on the proposed 25% re-phasing and the Net 60 ask?

Next steps I propose:
1) Kimberly to confirm whether the 25% step-down language is acceptable from a legal/precedent perspective.
2) Ben to propose invoice cadence that satisfies AP (2 invoices) while keeping Redwood accounting clarity.
3) I’ll update the draft order form and circulate a redline.

We can set a 30-minute call if helpful — available Tue/Wed mornings.

Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[Attachment referenced: Finnova_OrderForm_Redlines_v1.pdf]

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finnova.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 17:38:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Draft order form – a few redlines and tax question

Thanks — quick legal read below. I took a conservative approach and proposed text that preserves Redwood’s revenue recognition and audit trail while giving Finnova the operational flexibility they’ve asked for.

Key points:
- Minimum commit re-phasing: we can accept a single one-time re-phasing after Q2 up to 25% provided Finnova provides 30 days’ written notice and the re-phased amount is amortized for revenue recognition across the remaining term. I added explicit language requiring a joint sign-off by finance leads (Redwood AP / Finnova AP).

- Discounts & overages: I agree we should be explicit — discounts apply only to committed units. Overage language will include a 90-day notice if Finnova wants to convert overage into committed capacity (to preserve billing predictability).

- Net terms: Net 60 is acceptable for Finnova’s EU entity on the condition we put a Payment Plan Annex in the order form that clarifies invoicing cadence and assigns late fee appetite (no SLA credits apply while payment is outstanding). This protects Redwood cashflow.

- VAT / withholding: Redwood will provide standard VAT invoices. If Finnova requests reverse charge (customer accounts for VAT), we need their VAT registration and confirmation in writing. Withholding taxes — we’ll need country-by-country evidence if Finnova claims Redwood should gross-up.

I’ve prepared a short redline (attached) and a two-column summary table with the contractual language (legal text vs. commercial intent).

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Redline_Summary_Table.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finnova.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 09:14:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Draft order form – a few redlines and tax question

Oliver / team —pricing/ops perspective below and a proposed invoice flow attached. Main goal: meet AP’s ask for two invoices while keeping our collections process simple.

Proposed invoice cadence (commercial compromise):
1) Invoice A (Upfront credit): Issued at signing for the committed units' first quarter value (applies as a credit over the first 3 months).
2) Invoice B (Quarterly true-up): Issued at the end of each quarter for actual usage vs committed; shows credit applied and any overage billing.

Net terms: we can set Net 60 for Finnova EU invoices, with an internal credit check and a rolling review every 6 months. If a payment becomes >45 days overdue, Redwood reserves the right to suspend access with 14 days’ notice.

VAT: we will include VAT on invoices as required. For reverse-charge requests, AP should confirm the VAT ID and we’ll flag the invoice accordingly.

Attachments: Invoice_Flow_Proposed.pdf (diagram) and an example invoice layout.

Action items for close:
- Oliver: confirm acceptance of Invoice A/B cadence and provide VAT / legal entity info.
- Diego: update the order form with Kimberly’s re-phasing clause and Ben’s invoice cadence; then we send final redline for sign-off.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Commercials Lead, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Invoice_Flow_Proposed.pdf (pdf)]

From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finnova.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: Accounts Payable <ap@finnova.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 15:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Draft order form – a few redlines and tax question

Diego / Kimberly / Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear options. AP is happy with the two-invoice approach and the Net 60 term for the EU entity — they will send us the VAT ID and the internal PO reference by end of day tomorrow.

We do have one small ask on the re-phasing language: can the notice period be shortened from 30 days to 14 days? Their operations team says they can provide accurate usage numbers quickly and prefer a faster turnaround. If Redwood keeps the amortization requirement, they can accept a 14-day notice.

If that’s acceptable I’ll get formal sign-off from our CFO and instruct AP to process Invoice A once the DocuSign envelope is live.

Oliver
